evidence.finding: Routing configuration version 24.7 was deployed to all queues at 09:15, coincident with the incident start.
Aggregate transfer rate rose from 6.49% at 09:00 to 12.23% at 09:15 and remained near 12–13% through 11:45.
Aggregate AHT increased from 382.7 seconds at 09:00 to 505.4 seconds at 09:15 and remained between approximately 501 and 525 seconds thereafter, materially above forecasts near 371–381 seconds.
Service level fell from 85.3% at 09:00 to 50.6% at 09:15 and remained below the 80% target in most subsequent intervals until 11:45.
ASA increased from 27.6 seconds at 09:00 to 73.5 seconds at 09:15 and remained elevated during most of the incident.
After deployment, service levels deteriorated across queues with interval-specific severe results, including General Service at 44.7%, Account Support at 30.0%, and Escalations at 40.0% at 10:00.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49, with productive staffing generally stable at 45–46 agents and no agents in training.

Post-start offered demand averaged about 80 calls per interval versus approximately 76 forecast, a moderate increase that added pressure but was insufficient to explain the abrupt operational step change.

primary_root_cause_detail: Routing configuration version 24.7 was deployed across all queues at 09:15, exactly when transfer rates approximately doubled and AHT increased by roughly one-third. With staffing and adherence stable, the resulting loss of throughput drove higher waits, abandonment, and sustained service-level degradation.
recommended_actions: Roll back or remediate routing configuration version 24.7 and compare routing rules with the prior production version.
Audit post-deployment destination selection, skill mappings, transfer loops, and escalation paths across all queues.
Add deployment guardrails that automatically compare transfer rate, AHT, ASA, and service level against pre-deployment baselines and trigger rollback on material step changes.
Temporarily rebalance capacity or activate overflow routing while queues recover, accounting for the moderate demand above forecast.
Validate recovery by confirming transfer rates and AHT return near pre-deployment levels before closing the incident.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Demand after 09:15 was only moderately above forecast and included multiple at- or below-forecast intervals; it did not exhibit a surge matching the abrupt, sustained doubling of transfers and rise in AHT.
All 49 scheduled agents remained logged in, productive staffing stayed near 45–46, and queue staffed-agent counts were unchanged.
Adherence remained approximately 91.8–93.9% through nearly the entire incident and did not decline at 09:15.
No agents were recorded in training during any interval.
AHT was a major direct mechanism, but its sudden onset alongside the routing deployment and transfer-rate increase makes it a downstream effect rather than the deepest supported cause.
No platform event was reported; the only coincident operational event was the routing deployment.
Forecast demand was modestly low, but forecast AHT was stable and the observed performance break occurred exactly with the routing change rather than through a broad forecast miss.
Reported service levels reconcile with the supplied formula, and offered calls reconcile with answered plus abandoned calls.

stakeholder_summary: CC-004 was caused by routing configuration version 24.7. Its 09:15 deployment coincided with an immediate doubling of transfer rates and a sustained AHT increase, reducing throughput despite stable staffing. Moderately above-forecast demand added pressure but was not the primary cause.
